findings.citation: D. Minic, "From quantum foundations of quantum field theory, string theory and quantum gravity to dark matter and dark energy", talk at the 10th Mathematical Physics Meeting, Belgrade; proceedings p. 183 (2020); arXiv:2003.00318 (conference proceedings)
findings.summary: Earliest explicit statement found (arXiv, 29 Feb 2020). In the metastring framework (Born geometry, modular spacetime) every Standard Model field has a dual field tied to the dual spacetime x̃; the duals are proposed as the dark-matter sector, and after integrating over x̃ visible and dual (dark) matter both live in the observed spacetime. Born reciprocity is invoked as requiring symmetric structures in spacetime and energy-momentum space, selecting 'Standard Model and its dual'. The metaparticle character of these quanta is offered as a possible reason detectors have seen nothing.
findings.difference: Same identification, different framework and different coupling. (1) Framework: metastring theory, a string-theoretic Born geometry in which spacetime x and the dual spacetime x̃ do not commute (scale λ) and every field is doubled; reciprocity is built into the formulation, not an exact symmetry broken spontaneously by a vacuum-selected polarization with η as order parameter (#11 P2′, P5). (2) Coupling: the dual (dark) sector is 'correlated'/'entangled' with visible matter through non-gravitational terms and is tied to modified dark matter's acceleration-scale correlation with baryons; the school expects it to be detectable. C1 under strict P4 couples the sectors only through gravity and predicts a permanent direct-detection null (#11 §4, §13 row 7). (3) No velocity-gated self-interaction (the χ form) and no monopole form (C2). (4) Dark energy there is the curvature of the dual spacetime, not the program's τ. Here the dual quanta are also identified with 'modified dark matter' (MDM) and 'should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter'; C1 says the opposite (no non-gravitational coupling).

findings.difference: Dark matter extended in both position and momentum, not organized in momentum as a mirror polarization; charged non-local excitations would couple to photons (C1 forbids gauge crossing); no gate. Its non-detection argument resembles C3's logic.

So the school's 'dual' sector is the sector of the other polarization, which is what C1 calls conjugate matter. The paper itself says nothing about dark matter.

findings.summary: A model realizing Born reciprocity (the trans-Planckian theory) with gravity, one gauge field and one matter field identified with dark matter. The dark matter is an ordinary cold particle (WIMP-like); the dual part of its action, suppressed by inflation, becomes relevant at late times and acts as an effective cosmological constant.
findings.difference: Dark matter is not the reciprocal counterpart of ordinary matter; the dual sector of the dark-matter field produces dark energy. Bears more on C5 than on C1.

quotes.text: This is possible just considering a simple model that contains gravity, one gauge field plus one matter field (to be identified with dark matter), together with the reciprocity principle.

The most intriguing prediction of the new approach is the possible existence of exotic fermions with no analogues in the SM, which may be candidate for dark matter constituents.

findings.summary: Biconformal space has the structure of relativistic phase space (symplectic form, orthogonal Lagrangian submanifolds for configuration and momentum); geometric terms on the configuration submanifold act as a cosmological constant and a dust-like fluid, offered as dark-energy and dark-matter candidates.
findings.difference: The dark-matter candidate is a geometric term, not matter of the conjugate polarization; nearer the program's X-condensate idea (dark sector from geometry) than to C1.

quotes.text: We show that the general solution posesses orthogonal Lagrangian submanifolds
these new geometric features provide novel candidates for dark energy and dark matter

findings.citation: L. Marzola, M. Raidal, F. R. Urban, "Oscillating Spin-2 Dark Matter", Phys. Rev. D 97, 024010 (2018), doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.97.024010; arXiv:1708.04253 (journal)
findings.summary: Bears on the program's X-condensate candidate (not one of P.R.'s conjectures): a coherent oscillation of the massive spin-2 field of bimetric theory accounts for the dark-matter abundance, with its equation of motion and phenomenology computed, which the record says no program document has done.
findings.difference: Not about conjugate matter; it is published prior art for the X-condensate idea itself.

quotes.text: the coherent oscillations of a spin-2 field from bimetric theory can easily account for the observed dark matter abundance

findings.citation: M. Kaplinghat, S. Tulin, H.-B. Yu, "Dark Matter Halos as Particle Colliders: Unified Solution to Small-Scale Structure Puzzles from Dwarfs to Clusters", Phys. Rev. Lett. 116, 041302 (2016); arXiv:1508.03339 (journal)
findings.summary: Fits to halos from dwarfs to clusters prefer a mildly velocity-dependent self-interaction, about 2 cm²/g on galaxy scales falling to about 0.1 cm²/g on cluster scales. This bears on the χ form only: #11 §13 row 1 requires 'zero cluster signal (particle χ)' and a knee near 10² km/s.
findings.difference: Mild evidence: a preferred nonzero cluster-scale cross-section and a gentle velocity dependence sit uneasily with a sharp gate; the fits assume Yukawa-type mediators, are model-dependent, and do not amount to the 'robust self-interaction at v ≫ v*' that row 1 lists as its kill condition. Whether a rational gate tail could match them is not assessed here. Says nothing on the core identification.

quotes.text: Our results prefer a mildly velocity-dependent cross section
on cluster scales, consistent with the upper limits from merging clusters

findings.citation: L. Sagunski, S. Gad-Nasr, B. Colquhoun, A. Robertson, S. Tulin, "Velocity-dependent Self-interacting Dark Matter from Groups and Clusters of Galaxies", JCAP 01 (2021) 024; arXiv:2006.12515 (journal)
findings.summary: Jeans analysis of relaxed groups and clusters gives a mild preference for a nonzero self-interaction (groups 0.5 ± 0.2 cm²/g, clusters 0.19 ± 0.09 cm²/g, per the abstract), consistent with a cross section that falls with velocity. Bears on the χ form's 'zero cluster signal' (#11 §13 row 1).
findings.difference: Mild preference, not a detection; supports velocity dependence in general while weighing slightly against a gate that is fully closed at group and cluster speeds. Says nothing on the core identification.

quotes.text: For both groups and clusters, our results show a mild preference for a nonzero cross section compared with cold collisionless dark matter.
but are consistent with a velocity-dependent cross section that decreases with increasing scattering velocity

findings.citation: F. Henry-Couannier, "The Dark Side of Gravity", Global J. Sci. Front. Res. A 13, 1 (2013); arXiv:gr-qc/0610079 (journal)
findings.summary: Uses 'conjugate matter' for matter on the time-reversed, negative-energy 'conjugate side' of a two-metric universe (after J.-P. Petit), proposed as an alternative to dark matter: a galaxy repels conjugate matter and the resulting void acts on us like a dark halo.
findings.difference: Same words, different thing: conjugate under time reversal and energy sign, not position–momentum; the effect is repulsion, not a second polarization gravitating like ours.

quotes.text: he could show that conjugate matter is a powerful alternative idea to dark matter or dark energy
of course it’s just normal matter but on the conjugate side of our universe

findings.citation: D. V. Ahluwalia, D. Grumiller, "Spin half fermions with mass dimension one: Theory, phenomenology, and dark matter", JCAP 07 (2005) 012; arXiv:hep-th/0412080 (journal)
findings.summary: ELKO dark matter: 'dual-helicity eigenspinors of the charge conjugation operator', a mass-dimension-one fermion with quartic self-interaction, light (about 20 MeV), coupling to us via Higgs and gravity; the abstract also mentions 'energy-momentum space'.
findings.difference: 'Conjugation' is charge conjugation and 'dual' is helicity; a new spinor class, not momentum-polarized matter.

quotes.text: It is based upon a complete set of dual-helicity eigenspinors of the charge conjugation operator.
In a critique of the theory we bare a hint on non-commutative aspects of spacetime, and energy-momentum space.

findings.citation: S. Tremaine, J. E. Gunn, "Dynamical Role of Light Neutral Leptons in Cosmology", Phys. Rev. Lett. 42, 407 (1979) (journal)
findings.summary: The phase-space (Vlasov) density bound on fermionic dark matter in halos, which a reader searching 'dark matter organized in momentum/phase space' will meet first.
findings.difference: A bound on the maximum phase-space density of light fermions in halos; nothing to do with a momentum polarization of matter (and irrelevant at χ's benchmark mass scale).

quotes.text: Using the Vlasov equation, we show that massive galactic halos cannot be composed of stable neutral leptons

findings.citation: C. M. Ho, D. Minic, Y. J. Ng, "Cold Dark Matter with MOND Scaling", Phys. Lett. B 693, 567 (2010); arXiv:1005.3537 (journal)
findings.summary: 'Duality' between cold dark matter and MOND in the same school's earlier modified-dark-matter work.
findings.difference: A duality of descriptions (mass term versus acceleration law), not a dual matter sector.

quotes.text: We propose a duality between cold dark matter and modified Newtonian dynamics (MOND).

findings.citation: V. I. Tselyaev, "Dual relativity and its cosmological consequences", Phys. Rev. D 111, 104045 (2025); arXiv:2412.13400 (journal)
findings.summary: 'Ordinary' and 'dual' matter governed by two mutually dual metrics, with an antigravitational interaction between them; the dual matter is not proposed as dark matter.
findings.difference: 'Dual' is a vierbein duality between two metrics; the cross-interaction is repulsive.

quotes.text: In the TDR it is assumed that there exist two kinds of matter governed by the mutually dual physical metrics, and it is shown that the interaction between them has antigravitational character.

closest.why: Closest refereed statement of C1's core: Berglund, Hübsch and Minic (LHEP 2021) say in the abstract that dark matter 'comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter', the dual of each Standard Model field in the Born geometry of metastring theory, where the dual space is the 'canonically conjugate dual space'. It differs from C1 in framework (metastring, intrinsic x–x̃ non-commutativity; no spontaneous breaking, no η order parameter), in coupling (the dual sector is correlated with visible matter by non-gravitational terms and 'provides sources' for it, against strict P4's gravity-only coupling and permanent null), and in content (no velocity-gated self-interaction, no monopoles). The same school repeats the claim in IJMPD 32 (2023) 2330002, a paper the record already cites for dark energy.

Earliest explicit statement found (29 Feb 2020): Minic ties the identification to Born reciprocity between spacetime and energy-momentum space ('Standard Model and its dual, describing the dark matter sector'), and offers the metaparticle nature of the dual quanta as a possible reason for null detection. Differences as above; in addition he expects the dual quanta to be detectable through their entanglement with visible matter.

For the χ form's gate only: no paper was found that ties a self-interaction acting only between particles of nearly equal velocity to momentum-space structure. The nearest published content is the velocity-dependent self-interaction inferred from halos (Kaplinghat, Tulin, Yu 2016), produced there by ordinary Yukawa mediators and mildly falling with velocity rather than gated.

not_found.statement: Dark matter as matter of the momentum polarization in a framework where Born reciprocity is exact and spontaneously broken (the vacuum selects the polarization; η is the order parameter), with the two polarizations sharing gravity and no gauge force crossing between them, hence a permanent direct-detection null. The identification itself is published (metastring school, 2020–2026); this spontaneous-breaking, gravity-only version of it was not found.

notes: Main result: the core of C1, that dark matter is the reciprocal (Born-dual) counterpart of ordinary matter, the same kind of matter in the other polarization and gravitating with ours, is published. The Freidel–Leigh–Minic school says it from February 2020 on: Minic 2020 (Belgrade proceedings), Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2020 (LHEP 2021, abstract), Edmonds–Minic–Takeuchi 2021 (MG16), the 2022 Snowmass paper, BHM 2023 (IJMPD 32 2330002, already cited by the record for dark energy), BHM 2023 (Symmetry), Jejjala–Kavic–Minic–Tze (IJMPA 2022), Hübsch–Minic 2024 and 2026. In their words the whole Standard Model has a dual Standard Model, and that dual is the dark-matter sector. FLM's own papers of 2013–2019 never mention dark matter (full texts of 1307.7080, 1405.3949, 1502.08005, 1606.01829, 1706.03305, 1707.00312 and 1812.10821 retrieved and grepped for 'dark'); FLM 2017 (J. Phys. Conf. Ser.) only expects 'implications ... for the problems of dark matter', and FKLM 2021 says dual degrees of freedom 'may play the role of dark energy/matter'. The 2017 MDM review is a precursor (metaparticles as dark-matter quanta). Why 'anticipates' and not 'related': in this framework 'dual' means the Born-reciprocal partner. FLM define Born reciprocity as the space–momentum symmetry and spacetime as a choice of polarization, BHM call the dual space 'canonically conjugate', and Minic grounds the dual Standard Model in Born reciprocity between spacetime and energy-momentum space. So the school's dual matter is matter of the other polarization, as C1's conjugate matter is. What the school does not have, and what may still be C1's own: (a) the spontaneous-breaking setting (vacuum-selected polarization, η as order parameter); (b) strict P4, gravity-only coupling and a permanent direct-detection null, where the school instead has visible–dark correlation terms, ties its dark matter to MOND-like scaling (MDM), expects it to be detectable, and later makes it 'fuzzy'; (c) the χ form's self-interaction gated in relative velocity, of which nothing was found anywhere; (d) the monopole form (C2). Evidence bearing on the χ form: two halo analyses (Kaplinghat–Tulin–Yu 2016; Sagunski et al. 2021) mildly prefer a nonzero cluster-scale self-interaction, which sits uneasily with row 1's 'zero cluster signal' but is not the 'robust' signal row 1 names as its kill condition. Structural precedents of C1's shape (a copy of our matter meeting ours mainly through gravity): mirror matter (Foot; Berezhiani; Mohapatra–Nussinov–Teplitz), twin matter on the second metric of bigravity (Aoki–Maeda 2014; Hossenfelder 2008, whose twins repel; Petit's negative masses). Other reciprocity-based dark-matter ideas differ in kind: Bolognesi (dual action of an ordinary dark-matter field makes dark energy), Castro Perelman (dark matter as an accelerating-frame effect), Delbourgo–Lashmar (rotation curves without dark matter), Kadyshevsky et al. (exotic fermions from de Sitter momentum space). For the X-condensate (not P.R.'s): Marzola–Raidal–Urban, PRD 97 024010 (2018), compute dark matter as coherent oscillations of the bimetric spin-2 field, and Aoki–Mukohyama, PRD 96 104039 (2017), get the dark-matter/baryon ratio with massive-graviton dark matter. Flag 20 is confirmed: INSPIRE gives 'Bigravitational origin of dark matter' as arXiv:1604.08564 (PRD 94 084055), while arXiv:1607.03497 is 'Heavy spin-2 Dark Matter' (JCAP 09 (2016) 016); #11 reference [23] pairs the first title with the second number. Leads for other groups: Bolognesi 2012 writes a dual FRW universe in energy–momentum coordinates with its own expansion factor (C5, a·ã = 1); Minic 2020 and Chang et al. 2016 explain null detection by non-locality (C3's logic); Berezhiani's asymmetric mirror baryogenesis bears on the 5.4 : 1 question. Method: 101 database queries logged automatically (queries.jsonl), plus 11 WebSearch/WebFetch entries; one arXiv query hit HTTP 429 and was rerun. Every quote reported was checked with lit.py quote (all FOUND) except one from a PDF read through WebFetch. Working files are in work/literature-check/g1-conjugate-matter/.
